summary: The note gives a brief overview of the history of Buddhism, which spans from the 5th century BCE to the present. It explains that Buddhism arose in eastern Ancient India around the Kingdom of Magadha and is based on the teachings of Siddhārtha Gautama. The note describes how the religion spread across Asia, influencing most of the continent, and notes the development of many movements and schools, including Theravāda, Mahāyāna and Vajrayāna, amid periods of expansion and retreat.
one_line: Overview of Buddhism's history from the 5th century BCE, its origins in ancient Magadha, its spread across Asia, and its major traditions.
key_facts: The history of Buddhism spans from the 5th century BCE to the present.
Buddhism arose in the eastern part of Ancient India, in and around the ancient Kingdom of Magadha.
The ancient Kingdom of Magadha is now in Bihar, India.
Buddhism is based on the teachings of Siddhārtha Gautama.
Buddhism is one of the oldest religions practiced today.
The religion evolved as it spread from the northeastern region of the Indian subcontinent through Central, East, and Southeast Asia.
At one time or another, Buddhism influenced most of the Asian continent.
The history of Buddhism is characterized by the development of numerous movements, schisms, and schools.
The Theravāda tradition is one of the major traditions named in the history of Buddhism.
The Mahāyāna tradition is one of the major traditions named in the history of Buddhism.
The Vajrayāna tradition is one of the major traditions named in the history of Buddhism.
The history of Buddhism has featured contrasting periods of expansion and retreat.
